title: Introduce workload replay-based batch defaults and incremental quant-tiering
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: production teams repeatedly tune batching/caching defaults and quantization profiles by hand for specific workloads. Those ad-hoc defaults drift, are brittle, and either increase latency or miss cost savings. This PR implements a pragmatic, automated path: derive conservative per-route batching/caching defaults from sampled production traces (replay sampler) and introduce an incremental quant-tierer that safely experiments with lower-precision model variants in shadow mode before gradual rollout.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a replay-based sampler that consumes anonymized request traces and computes distributional summaries (sequence length, token arrival spacing, request concurrency) used to generate recommended batch_size, max_latency_target, and prefill thresholds per-route.
- Implements an incremental quant-tierer engine that can schedule shadow runs of quantized variants (q4/q5 candidates) and compute output divergence metrics, token-level latency/cost delta, and rollout risk scores. The tierer supports staged rollouts with automatic rollback on quality regressions.
- Hooks telemetry: unit-cost-per-route, shadow-comparison drift metrics, rollout success rate, and a small dashboard surface in the Console to inspect suggested profiles and accept/reject rollouts.
- Adds a CLI helper to run local replays against a dev runtime for validation.

Checklist:
- [x] Replay sampler implementation (runtime/batcher/replay_sampler.py)
- [x] Quant tierer core and scheduler (optimizer/quant_tierer.go)
- [x] Shadow run plumbing and comparison metrics (runtime/shadow_proxy.rs)
- [x] Console UI for profile suggestions and rollout control (console/ui/workload-profiles.tsx)
- [x] Integration tests that run a small synthetic trace and validate recommended defaults (tests/integration/test_replay_defaults.py)
- [x] Unit tests for quant comparison metrics and rollback logic (tests/unit/test_quant_tierer.go)
- [x] Minimal docs: docs/ops/replay-and-quant-tiering.md

Migration & safety notes:
- Defaults produced by the sampler are recommendations only; they do not override existing explicit per-customer configs unless an engineer or admin accepts them from the Console.
- The quant-tierer is opt-in per route. Rollouts use shadow traffic first, then small-percentage live traffic ramps. All rollouts are reversible and monitored.

Why it's different from prior autotuners: instead of global heuristics we compute workload-shaped defaults using real traces and couple that with a conservative, staged quant rollout flow that measures quality at token- and sequence-levels before promoting a quant tier. The focus is on minimizing false positives (bad rollouts) while surfacing clear unit-econ impact to engineers.

release_notes: Add workload replay-based batching/caching recommendations and an opt-in incremental quant-tierer with shadow runs and staged rollouts. Exposes per-route suggested defaults in Console. Opt-in only; defaults are not auto-applied.
testing_notes: Integration harness includes a synthetic 10k-request trace with variable sequence lengths and concurrency shapes. The replay-runner CLI makes it easy to validate suggestions locally. Tests validate PII stripping, divergence metrics, rollback on quality degradation (>2% normalized edit distance increase), and that shadow runs show <=1.5x latency overhead in dev mode.
